title: What If the Higgs Field Switched Off?

scenes.text: What if the Higgs field switched off? Your atoms would stop existing.
The Higgs field fills all of space. Electrons and quarks get their mass by interacting with it.
Switch it off, and a massless electron can only travel one way: at the speed of light.
The Nobel committee put it bluntly: all matter would collapse as the suddenly massless electrons dispersed at light speed.
No atoms means no molecules. No water, no rock, no cells. Chemistry itself would stop.
Physicist Matt Strassler estimates atoms would swell to about a trillion times their size. Matter exists only because one invisible field stays on.
